source.repro: JEST_MAX_WORKERS=<n> npx jest --ci --silent, whole suite, warm transform cache, on an otherwise idle 16-core / 30GB Linux box. Peak memory is the largest total RSS over all processes matching 'jest', sampled every 2s for the length of the run. Sigma per-suite is the sum of (endTime - startTime) over every entry in --json's testResults.
source.notes: Taken after the 2026-08-30 harness changes, so it is the curve the maxWorkers ceiling in jest.config.js is set from rather than a before/after. All four runs were green over the same 1975 suites and 20,504 tests. The measurement this replaces was taken over `packages/core/src/util` alone and concluded worker count did not matter: its suites are ~0.1s each, so that run was reading jest's ~3.5s of startup, which no worker count divides. Read the whole suite. Workers stay ~97% occupied at every count, so the suite parallelises; what stops scaling is the per-suite cost under contention, which is why Sigma per-suite grows down the table while wall clock flattens. Wall clock on this box moves a few percent run to run, so the 12-vs-16 pair is a tie rather than a reversal. PREDATES the test-file pass later the same day, which took a same-box 4-worker run from 346s/1305s to 291s/1120s; that pass moves every row down by roughly a seventh and the curve is unchanged, but the absolute numbers here are the ones measured before it. Re-take the whole table on an idle box rather than scaling it.
